question.problem: Three factories produce the same tool for the market. Factory $A$ produces $30%$ of the tools, of which $2%$ are defective. Factory $B$ produces $34%$ of the tools, of which $5%$ are defective, and factory $C$ produces $36%$ of the tools, of which $5%$ are defective. What is the probability that a randomly selected tool is defective?
question.worked_solution:
Let $D$ be the event that a randomly selected tool is defective, and 

- let $A$ be the event that the tool was produced by factory $A,$

- let $B$ be the event that the tool was produced by factory $B,$

- let $C$ be the event that the tool was produced by factory $C.$

Then the disjoint union $A⊔B⊔C$ covers the entire sample space.

To calculate the probability that a randomly selected tool is defective, we can use the law of total probability:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(D) & =P(D\cap A)+P(D\cap B)+P(D\cap C) \\  & =P(D|A)P(A)+P(D|B)P(B)+P(D|C)P(C)\end{aligned}
$$

Let's go through the problem statement and translate each piece of information into mathematical notation.

- Since factory $A$ produces $30%$ of the tools, factory $B$ produces $34%$ of the tools, and factory $C$ produces $36%$ of the tools, we have

$$
P(A)=0.3,\,P(B)=0.34,\,P(C)=0.36.
$$

- Since $2%$ of the tools produced by factory $A$, $5%$ of the tools produced by factory $B$, and $5%$ of the tools produced by factory $C,$ are defective, we have 

$$
P(D|A)=0.02,\,P(D|B)=0.05,\,P(D|C)=0.05.
$$

Substituting the above information into the law of total probability, the probability that a randomly selected tool is defective is

$$
\begin{aligned}P(D) & =P(D|A)P(A)+P(D|B)P(B)+P(D|C)P(C) \\  & =(0.02)(0.3)+(0.05)(0.34)+(0.05)(0.36) \\  & =0.006+0.017+0.018 \\  & =0.041.\end{aligned}
$$
